# TabDisplay

<!-- docs:begin summary -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

TabDisplay formats Java player-list names, headers, and footers. It leaves Bedrock lists unchanged.
<!-- docs:end summary -->

<!-- docs:begin reference -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs from package, action, extension, and component docs metadata. Run `pnpm readme`. -->

See the [plugin guide](https://filiphsps.github.io/pumpkin-plugins/packages/tab-display/docs/) and [API reference](https://filiphsps.github.io/pumpkin-plugins/api/plugins/tab-display/) on the documentation site.
<!-- docs:end reference -->

## Installation

<!-- docs:begin installation -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

TabDisplay hasn't been released yet, so there is no `tab-display.wasm` to download. Its player-list changes haven't been checked with a Java client yet. To try it, clone this repository, run `pnpm build --filter @pumpkin-plugins/tab-display`, copy `build/tab-display.wasm` from the plugin's folder to your server's `plugins/` folder, and restart Pumpkin.
<!-- docs:end installation -->

PumpkinPIE placeholders are optional and come from a separate external plugin. TabDisplay does not
build or bundle PumpkinPIE; install a compatible provider from the
[PumpkinPIE releases](https://github.com/Rennex07/PumpkinPIE/releases).

## Permissions

<!-- docs:begin permissions -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

Pumpkin asks you to approve these on the server console when it loads the plugin. It skips the question when the `[plugins]` table in `pumpkin.toml` lists all of them in `allowed_permissions` or sets `ask_permission_confirmation = false`. Pumpkin remembers your answer and asks again after the plugin file or this list changes.

| Permission | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `fs.read.data` | Read TabDisplay settings from the plugin data folder. |
| `fs.write.data` | Create and update TabDisplay settings in the plugin data folder. |
| `http.outbound` | Check Pumpkin Market for plugin updates. |
<!-- docs:end permissions -->

## Commands

<!-- docs:begin commands -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

| Command | Description | Permission | Default access |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/tabdisplay status` | Show PumpkinPIE state, players and recent problems | `TabDisplay:command.status` | operators (level 3) |
| `/tabdisplay reload` | Reload config.toml | `TabDisplay:command.reload` | operators (level 3) |
| `/tabdisplay inspect <player>` | Show a player's placeholder IDs | `TabDisplay:command.inspect` | operators (level 3) |
<!-- docs:end commands -->

## Configuration

<!-- docs:begin config -->
<!-- Generated by pumpkin-plugins-docs. Edit src/info.ts, then run `pnpm readme`. -->

Settings live in `plugins/data/TabDisplay/config.toml`. The plugin creates the file if needed, adds settings from the schema and removes settings no longer defined there. Values for existing settings are preserved.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `general.version` | integer | `1` | Format version. Do not change this value. |
| `general.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Apply configured Java tab display changes. |
| `general.refresh_ticks` | integer | `20` | Ticks between full display refreshes. |
| `general.max_players` | integer | `500` | Maximum player snapshots processed per refresh. |
| `placeholders.provider` | string | `"PumpkinPIE"` | Pumpkin plugin that supplies placeholder values. |
| `placeholders.missing_provider` | string | `"literal"` | Text to show for tokens other than `%player_name%` and `%server_online%` when PumpkinPIE is unavailable: `literal` keeps them, `empty` removes them. |
| `placeholders.unresolved` | string | `"literal"` | Text to show for unresolved identifiers: `literal` keeps tokens, `empty` removes them. |
| `header.lines` | table[] | `[{ text = "Welcome %player_name%", color = "#FFB347" }]` | Header lines in display order. Use a TOML array of inline tables, for example [{ text = "Welcome %player_name%", color = "#FFB347" }]. |
| `footer.lines` | table[] | `[{ text = "%server_online% players online", color = "#AAAAAA" }]` | Footer lines in display order. Use a TOML array of inline tables, for example [{ text = "%server_online% players online", color = "#AAAAAA" }]. |
| `entry.enabled` | boolean | `true` | Apply a custom name to real player rows. |
| `entry.text` | string | `"%player_name%"` | Name template for each listed player. |
| `entry.color` | string | `"#FFFFFF"` | RGB text color in `#RRGGBB` form. |
| `entry.bold` | boolean | `false` | Render the row name in bold. |
| `entry.italic` | boolean | `false` | Render the row name in italics. |
| `entry.underlined` | boolean | `false` | Underline the row name. |
| `entry.strikethrough` | boolean | `false` | Strike through the row name. |

<details>
<summary>A fresh install gets this file:</summary>

```toml
# TabDisplay configuration.
# This file is managed by the plugin: when it starts, settings that were added are written here with
# their defaults and settings that were removed are dropped. Your values are kept; comments you add
# are not. Changes apply after `/tabdisplay reload` or a server restart.

# Plugin refresh and workload limits.
[general]

# Format version. Do not change this value.
version = 1

# Apply configured Java tab display changes.
enabled = true

# Ticks between full display refreshes.
refresh_ticks = 20

# Maximum player snapshots processed per refresh.
max_players = 500

# PumpkinPIE placeholder handling.
[placeholders]

# Pumpkin plugin that supplies placeholder values.
provider = "PumpkinPIE"

# Text to show for tokens other than `%player_name%` and `%server_online%` when PumpkinPIE is
# unavailable: `literal` keeps them, `empty` removes them.
missing_provider = "literal"

# Text to show for unresolved identifiers: `literal` keeps tokens, `empty` removes them.
unresolved = "literal"

# Personalized header lines. Each player sees their own placeholder context.
[header]

# Header lines in display order. Use a TOML array of inline tables, for example [{ text = "Welcome
# %player_name%", color = "#FFB347" }].
lines = [{ text = "Welcome %player_name%", color = "#FFB347" }]

# Personalized footer lines. Each player sees their own placeholder context.
[footer]

# Footer lines in display order. Use a TOML array of inline tables, for example [{ text =
# "%server_online% players online", color = "#AAAAAA" }].
lines = [{ text = "%server_online% players online", color = "#AAAAAA" }]

# Global real-player row formatting. Placeholder context is the listed subject.
[entry]

# Apply a custom name to real player rows.
enabled = true

# Name template for each listed player.
text = "%player_name%"

# RGB text color in `#RRGGBB` form.
color = "#FFFFFF"

# Render the row name in bold.
bold = false

# Render the row name in italics.
italic = false

# Underline the row name.
underlined = false

# Strike through the row name.
strikethrough = false
```
</details>
<!-- docs:end config -->
